title: Paperclip AI: what it is, whether it's reliable and how to host it on Hostinger
seoTitle: Paperclip AI: is it reliable? Managed or VPS on Hostinger
description: Paperclip is an open-source (MIT) orchestrator for teams of AI agents. See what you can verify and whether managed or a VPS on Hostinger is the better fit.

contentSections.heading: Quick answer
paragraphs: Paperclip organizes a team of AI agents, with roles, goals and a spending cap for each one, but it does not run the AI: the keys are yours. On Hostinger, it runs on the managed plan or on a VPS. What changes the decision is who looks after the server; see the comparison below.

contentSections.heading: What Paperclip is, in plain language
paragraphs: Paperclip is a program for organizing a team of AI agents: instead of a single assistant, you build the team with roles, goals and a spending cap for each agent. Think of a small company. There is an owner, managers and employees, each with their own job. Paperclip does the same with AI agents: each agent has a role, a job description and a boss. Whoever is above delegates tasks, and whoever is below answers to them. In the documentation, five ideas show up in the project.

image.alt: Board with a Goal at the top, a CEO below it and three agents (Engineering, Marketing and Support), with a Budget and approval strip at the bottom
image.caption: How Paperclip organizes agents, according to the official documentation.

bullets: **Org chart:** the structure of who reports to whom. A marketing agent answers to whoever handles strategy, and so on.

**Heartbeats:** the name comes from “heartbeat”. An agent does not run all the time. It “wakes up” when it gets work, a follow-up message or a schedule, checks what it has to do and acts. Then it goes back to sleep.

**Budget per agent:** you set a spending cap for each agent, each project and the company. When the limit is reached, the work is paused. This matters because every AI response costs money, charged by the model provider.
**Approval:** you can require a review before a piece of work moves on, approve the hiring of a new agent or stop and reassign a task.
**Audit:** actions, state changes, costs, approvals and comments are all recorded. You can see afterwards what happened and why.
postParagraphs: The difference from a single agent is in the format. An assistant like [OpenClaw](/en/reviews/openclaw-hostinger-managed-or-vps) is a digital person you talk to, from start to finish. Paperclip is the meeting room: you define the roles and let the team work under budget and approval rules. For personal use, a single agent is usually enough. A team makes sense when there are several lines of work and you want to control the spending on each.

contentSections.heading: Is it reliable? What you can verify
paragraphs: “Reliable” is a big word. You can separate what is verifiable from what is not.

**Who maintains it.** The official repository, github.com/paperclipai/paperclip, says the project is maintained by the Paperclip team, and the copyright notice reads “MIT © 2026 Paperclip Labs, Inc.”. The project’s website, paperclip.ing, points to the same repository. Do not confuse it with the forks and copies of the code that show up in search.
**License.** MIT. It means the code is open: anyone can read it, audit it and use it. It also means nobody is obliged to keep maintaining the version you installed.

**Where it runs.** You choose. It can run on your computer, on a server of your own or on Hostinger’s managed plan. The project’s website says the self-hosted version does not require a Paperclip account.

**Where the keys and data live.** It depends on the path. On the VPS, Hostinger itself says that sensitive data, agent memory and API credentials stay “entirely on your infrastructure”, that is, on the server you rented. On managed, the page says the keys stay in your managed instance. This is Hostinger’s description, not an audit of ours.

**Code security.** The repository asks that vulnerabilities be reported through GitHub’s Security Advisory feature, not in public issues. In this reading, we did not check supported versions, independent audits or published advisories.

**What cannot be claimed.** There is no verified public security audit for this guide. There is also no independent review or third-party rating for the product. The number of stars on GitHub shows popularity, not security. An agent with access to your email, your bank or other accounts deserves extra care, whatever the software. For the company that hosts it, see [whether Hostinger is trustworthy](/en/reviews/is-hostinger-legit).

contentSections.heading: What you need to have
paragraphs: Before you sign up, check these five points.
bullets: **Agents to coordinate.** Paperclip does not run an AI model: it coordinates agents that work through other programs, such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and OpenClaw.

**Postgres.** This is the database where Paperclip stores agents, tasks and records. In the local install, it comes built in and starts on its own. In production, the project itself recommends pointing to a Postgres of your own. On managed, the database is included. On the VPS, the database is up to you.

**Your own AI keys.** An API key is the password the program uses to ask a provider for answers, such as Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI or another. The provider charges for usage, directly to you. The managed Paperclip page says you connect “your own agents and API keys”, and it does not list included AI credits. Without a key, the team does not answer.

**A monthly budget per agent.** Set the cap before you turn the team on. Five agents with daily tasks can spend far more than an assistant you chat with now and then. Without a cap, the spending is whatever the provider charges at the end of the month.

**Server knowledge, if you go with a VPS.** On a VPS, you need to know what Docker is, a program that runs each application isolated in a container, and accept updating and securing the system. If that is not for you, managed solves it.
postParagraphs: If you are going to run it locally, the project requires Node.js 24.11 or higher. Older versions of Node do not work.

contentSections.heading: Managed or VPS on Hostinger
paragraphs: The choice is who looks after the server: on **managed**, it is Hostinger, which also takes care of the database and the updates. On the **VPS**, you rent a virtual server, Hostinger installs Paperclip on it with Docker (a program that runs each application isolated in a container) and the rest is up to you.

postParagraphs: **Managed is for you if** you want Paperclip running without installing anything, you do not know what root or Docker is, and you prefer Hostinger to look after the database, the updates and the backups.

**The VPS is for you if** you want to run other programs on the same server, such as a website or n8n (an automation tool), you know your way around a server or want to learn, and you want the database and the configuration under your control.

On refunds, the 180-day rule for VPS is the same one in the [article on trusting Hostinger](/en/reviews/is-hostinger-legit), which reads the company’s policy. If you requested a VPS refund in the last six months, the new purchase does not have the 30-day guarantee.

contentSections.heading: What size of VPS
postParagraphs: RAM is the server’s memory, and a vCPU is one processor core. The bigger the VPS plan, the more memory and processing power it has. Hostinger does not list a minimum memory requirement for Paperclip on the pages read: the KVM 1 is the starting point, and how many agents you run decides whether it is enough. The plans are KVM 1 (1 vCPU, 4 GB, 50 GB), KVM 2 (2 vCPU, 8 GB, 100 GB), KVM 4 (4 vCPU, 16 GB, 200 GB) and KVM 8 (8 vCPU, 32 GB, 400 GB).

contentSections.heading: How to get started, in order
bullets: **Run it on your computer.** The official README requires Node.js 24.11 or newer. Check the version with the command node -v in the terminal, then run npx paperclipai@latest onboard --yes. The interface opens at http://localhost:3100, and the Postgres database is created on its own. There is no server cost, but Paperclip only runs while your computer is on. If you subscribe to Claude or Codex, the README also lets you sign in through the subscription, without an API key, with Python 3 and the provider’s program installed.

**Subscribe to managed.** Sign up for the “AI automation apps” plan for 24 months, with the code SONAR20 in the cart. After the subscription, Hostinger prepares the instance and the database. You log into the panel, connect your agents and paste in your AI keys.

**Or get a VPS with Docker.** Pick a KVM plan (the KVM 1 is the cheapest) and, in the list of applications, Paperclip, which Hostinger installs with one click. Through the panel’s Docker Manager you open Paperclip, enter the keys and update the version with a button. The server’s security, the passwords and the system updates remain yours.

contentSections.heading: Alternatives: a single agent
paragraphs: Paperclip organizes a team of agents. If you only want one assistant, for example on Telegram or WhatsApp, it is more than you need. For that choice, see [OpenClaw on Hostinger, managed or VPS](/en/reviews/openclaw-hostinger-managed-or-vps) and [OpenClaw or Hermes Agent](/en/reviews/openclaw-vs-hermes-agent), which compares the two single agents.

contentSections.heading: Frequently asked questions
bullets: Is Paperclip free? The program is open source, under the MIT license, and you can install it on your computer without paying Hostinger. The use of AI models is charged by the provider, and managed and the VPS are paid plans.

Is Paperclip reliable? No verdict can be given. What you can verify is that the code is public, that the repository names the Paperclip team (Paperclip Labs, Inc. in the copyright notice) as responsible, and that security flaws are reported through an official channel on GitHub. We found no independent audit in the sources read.
Does it need an API key? Yes. On managed and on the VPS, the Paperclip page asks you to bring your own. On your computer, the README also accepts a Claude or Codex subscription, without an API key.

Does it run with Ollama? It depends on the agent you connect. Paperclip’s README does not mention Ollama, a program for running an AI model on your own computer. OpenClaw, for example, documents local models; in Paperclip, the model stays with the agent you connect.
Is there a coupon for Paperclip on Hostinger? Yes: the code SONAR20, in the cart’s coupon field, gives 20% off the first period. We did not test the renewal; check the price in the cart.
